title: 2 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 7
description: Ten questions on 2 Corinthians 7: the comfort brought by the coming of Titus, the letter that caused grief, and godly sorrow that produces repentance.

questions.text: What does verse 1 call the beloved to do, having these promises?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says: let's cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

answers.text: To wait quietly until he comes to them again
To cleanse themselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit
To send a gift to the saints in Jerusalem
To write him a letter of commendation first

questions.text: What three things does the writer say about how he and his companions treated the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says: Open your hearts to us. We wronged no one. We corrupted no one. We took advantage of no one.

answers.text: They taught no one, judged no one, condemned no one
They asked nothing, received nothing, kept nothing
They visited no one, wrote to no one, sent no one
They wronged no one, corrupted no one, took advantage of no one

questions.text: What had he said before about the Corinthians being in their hearts?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says he had said before that they are in our hearts to die together and live together, and that he says this not to condemn them.

answers.text: That they are in their hearts to die together and live together
That they are their letter read by all men
That they are a temple of the living God
That they are the first fruits of Achaia

questions.text: What did they find when they had come into Macedonia, according to verse 5?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says their flesh had no relief, but they were afflicted on every side: fightings were outside, fear was inside.

answers.text: Rest and great joy on every side at last
A great and effective door opened to them
Affliction on every side, with fightings outside and fear inside
Many gifts from the assemblies in Macedonia

questions.text: By whose coming did God comfort them, according to verse 6?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says that he who comforts the lowly, God, comforted them by the coming of Titus.

answers.text: By the coming of Timothy
By the coming of Titus
By the coming of Apollos
By the coming of Stephanas

questions.text: What did Titus tell them about the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says Titus told them of the Corinthians' longing, their mourning, and their zeal for the writer, so that he rejoiced still more.

answers.text: Of their longing, their mourning, and their zeal for him
Of their wealth and their generosity
Of their divisions and their quarrels
Of their letters and their questions

questions.text: What does the writer say in verse 8 about the letter that grieved them?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says that though he grieved them with his letter, he does not regret it, though he did regret it, for he sees that his letter made them grieve just for a while.

answers.text: That he never wrote such a letter
That he wishes he had written more sharply
That he will send the same letter again
That he does not regret it, though he did regret it

questions.text: What does godly sorrow produce, and what does the sorrow of the world produce?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says godly sorrow produces repentance to salvation, which brings no regret, but the sorrow of the world produces death.

answers.text: Godly sorrow produces death, and worldly sorrow produces life
Both godly sorrow and worldly sorrow produce repentance to salvation
Godly sorrow produces repentance to salvation, but the sorrow of the world produces death
Neither godly nor worldly sorrow produces anything lasting

questions.text: Why did they rejoice the more exceedingly for the joy of Titus?
questions.explanation: Verse 13 says they rejoiced the more exceedingly for the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by them all.

answers.text: Because his spirit had been refreshed by them all
Because he had been given a gift by the assemblies
Because he had been set free from prison
Because he had been appointed to travel with them

questions.text: How does verse 15 say the Corinthians received Titus?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 says his affection is more abundantly toward them, while he remembers all of their obedience, how with fear and trembling they received him.

answers.text: With doubt and suspicion
With fear and trembling
With feasting and singing
With letters and gifts
